title: Fail-loud font guard is dead code: a missing TTF still silently runs the raylib default
evidence: view.odin:1353-1356: `font_load_data :: proc(path: string, size: i32, cps: []rune) -> (glyphs: [^]rl.GlyphInfo, count: c.int) {` / `data, err := os.read_entire_file_from_path(path, context.allocator)` — verbatim: `data, err := os.read_entire_file_from_path(path, context.temp_allocator)` / `if err != nil {` / `return nil, 0`. view.odin:1431-1435: `font_from_glyphs :: proc(glyphs: [^]rl.GlyphInfo, count: c.int, size: i32) -> rl.Font {` / `f: rl.Font` / `if glyphs == nil || count == 0 {` / `return rl.GetFontDefault()`. app/main.odin:317-318: `if !rl.IsFontValid(app.view.font) || !rl.IsFontValid(app.view.font_header) || !rl.IsFontValid(app.view.font_mono) {` / `fmt.eprintln("app: HUD font family failed to load (assets/fonts) - refusing to run with the raylib default")`. tools/raylib-sw/src/src/rtext.c:593-601 IsFontValid: `return ((font.baseSize > 0) &&      // Validate font size` / `(font.glyphCount > 0) &&    // Validate font contains some glyph` / `(font.recs != NULL) &&      // Validate font recs defining glyphs on texture atlas` / `(font.glyphs != NULL));     // Validate glyph data is loaded`. rtext.c:166 `defaultFont.glyphCount = 224; // Number of glyphs included in our default font`; rcore.c:710 `LoadFontDefault();` inside InitWindow; app InitWindow at main.odin:240 runs before load_fonts at 311, harness InitWindow at main.odin:347 before render_setup at 351.
detail: Missing asset → nil glyphs → font_from_glyphs returns GetFontDefault(), which passes IsFontValid (224 glyphs, loaded at InitWindow before load_fonts). The exit(2) guard can never fire — the silent-fallback lie stays possible.
recommended_fix: Return a zeroed (invalid) Font or a (Font, bool) from load_font_file on failure instead of GetFontDefault, so IsFontValid fails and the existing guards bite.

title: palette.json ink_soft edit violates the job's "palette unchanged" rule and guarantees non-text golden drift
evidence: data/palette.json:10: `  "ink_soft":      [66, 72, 80, 255],` (diff: `-  "ink_soft":      [92, 98, 106, 255],` → `+  "ink_soft":      [66, 72, 80, 255],`). Non-text consumers read in the worktree: app/main.odin:642 `rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx(chip, 1, p.ink_soft)`; app/main.odin:1847/1861 `rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx(r, 1, p.ink_soft)` (tray chip borders — drawn every frame); app/render/health.odin:67 `rl.DrawRectangle(bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, bar_h, p.ink_soft)`; app/render/settings_panel.odin:131 `rl.DrawRectangleLines(i32(r.x), i32(r.y), i32(r.width), i32(r.height), p.ink_soft)`; app/render/popover.odin:119 `rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx(r, 1, v.palette.ink_soft)`. Job briefing rule 6 (hard): "do NOT touch gameplay goldens beyond text pixels (palette/layout unchanged)".
detail: ink_soft is a shared token: besides text it colors tray-chip borders, the health bar track, settings/popover borders — non-text pixels present in essentially every golden. The re-bless diff bboxes cannot be text-band-only.
recommended_fix: Scope the 7.2:1 contrast to a new text token (e.g. ink_text_soft) in palette.json, revert ink_soft, or explicitly document the non-text drift as a second bless cause.

title: run_demo_to_ms added as a second copy of the replay driver; overlay_check keeps its own inline loop
evidence: harness/overlay.odin:73-78 (duplicated consecutive comment, read verbatim): `// run to the capture ms (wall ticks; paused wall ticks step nothing — the` / `// same driver the run path uses). The overlay renders the LAST stepped` / `// tick's state + its stats record + the event tail (the app's behavior).` / `hz := cat.balance.logic_hz` / `// run to the capture ms (wall ticks; paused wall ticks step nothing — the` / `// same driver the run path uses). ...` — followed by overlay_check's own inline wall-tick loop (for w in u64(1)..=wall_max ... pp.step). harness/overlay.odin:164: `run_demo_to_ms :: proc(state: ^pp.Run_State, d: ^Demo, cfg: ^Demo_Replay, cat: ^pp.Catalogs, cap_ms: i64) -> (sim_tick: u64, stats: pp.Stats_Record, stats_valid: bool) {`. harness/font_check.odin:160-161: `// 3. replay the demo to the capture ms (shared driver — the SAME sim` / `// path the overlay-check verb uses; the font swap never touches it).`

title: glyph_probe indexes the compacted glyph array by request index — misaligned verdicts and an OOB read for missing glyphs
evidence: harness/font_check.odin:62-65: `for i in 0..<n {` / `cp := cps[i]` / `g := f.glyphs[i]` / `present := g.advanceX > 0 || (g.image.width > 0 && g.image.height > 0)`. tools/raylib-sw/src/src/rtext.c:663-667 (LoadFontData): `if (index > 0) glyphCounter++;` ... `glyphs = (GlyphInfo *)RL_CALLOC(glyphCounter, sizeof(GlyphInfo));` — the array holds ONLY found glyphs (compaction); rtext.c:780 `*glyphCount = glyphCount;`. view.odin's own merge comment documents the same: "raylib COMPACTS the glyph array (missing codepoints are skipped; the atlas lookup maps by glyph.value, never by index".
detail: For a candidate missing any probed codepoint, glyphs[i] no longer corresponds to cps[i]: verdicts after the gap read the wrong glyph, and i=95 reads past the 95-entry array — the exact negative-control case.
recommended_fix: Look up by glyph value like font_probe_warning does (glyphs[i].value == cp), bound the loop by f.glyphCount, and reuse render.font_codepoints instead of duplicating build_probe_set.

title: Package-level mutable global `gallery: Gallery` violates the no-globals rule (ODN-13) and the sibling debug-tooling pattern
evidence: app/gallery.odin:63: `gallery: Gallery`. project-context.md (Critical Implementation Rules): "**No globals / singletons.** Everything hangs off `App` → `Run_State`, passed by pointer (ODN-13)." Sibling debug tooling keeps state on App: app/main.odin:181 `noc_e2e_frame: int,` (a field of the App struct), armed via `app.noc_e2e = os.get_env_alloc("PP_NOC_E2E", ...)`. grep over app/*.odin: `gallery: Gallery` is the only package-level mutable variable in the app package.
detail: First mutable package global in the app; the existing noc_e2e debug harness stores equivalent state as App fields. Diverges from ODN-13 and the established sibling pattern even inside PP_DEBUG code.
recommended_fix: Add the gallery state to App (PP_DEBUG-commented fields like noc_e2e) and pass &app.gallery, keeping the compile gate as-is.

title: palette.odin code fallbacks still carry the old ink_soft after palette.json moved — silent divergence on a failed palette load
evidence: app/render/palette.odin:200: `p.ink_soft = jcol(obj, "ink_soft", {92, 98, 106, 255})`; app/render/palette.odin:295: `p.ink_soft = {92, 98, 106, 255},`; data/palette.json:10: `  "ink_soft":      [66, 72, 80, 255],`. project-context.md (ODN-5): "Numbers single-source: balance numbers live in data/*.json, never restated in code".

title: font_merge_fallback leaks the fallback glyph array block (fg) it copies from
evidence: app/render/view.odin:1403-1404: `fg := rl.LoadFontData(raw_data(fdata), c.int(len(fdata)), size,` / `raw_data(missing[:missing_n]), c.int(missing_n), .DEFAULT, &ng)`; view.odin:1417-1421: `for j in 0..<ng {` / `merged[count + j] = fg[j]` / `}` / `rl.MemFree(glyphs) // the block is free; the glyph image data lives on in merged` — no MemFree(fg) anywhere in the proc. Its own comment claims: "UnloadFont owns every byte: the glyph structs AND their image data".
detail: Only the main block is freed; the fallback GlyphInfo array block (raylib RL_CALLOC) is orphaned each merge — three times per app/harness init plus per test probe. Small, one-time, but contradicts the ownership comment.
recommended_fix: Add `rl.MemFree(fg)` after the copy loop (before returning merged).

title: font-check probes the deleted Open Sans baseline — the comparison line can never load
evidence: harness/font_check.odin:158: `glyph_probe("assets/fonts/open_sans_regular.ttf", rnd.FONT_BASE_SIZE)`. The same diff deletes the file: `diff --git a/assets/fonts/open_sans_regular.ttf b/assets/fonts/open_sans_regular.ttf` / `deleted file mode 100644` / `index bba741a9..00000000`. assets/fonts/ in the worktree contains only the four Plex/Noto ttfs.
detail: The "this candidate + the baseline" probe hard-codes an asset removed in this same PR — every font-check run prints "cannot load" for the baseline instead of comparing anything.
recommended_fix: Point the baseline probe at a committed font (e.g. ibm_plex_sans_regular.ttf) or delete the baseline call.
